meta.description: Analyzes CRISPR drug-modifier (chemogenomic) screens with drugZ (Colic et al. 2019 Genome Med), a bidirectional Z-score method identifying synthetic-lethal sensitizing genes and resistance-conferring suppressor genes from vehicle vs drug comparisons.

scientific_integrity.detail: Citations (Colic et al. 2019 Genome Med, Olivieri et al. 2020 Cell, Behan et al. 2019 Nature) are real papers matching drugZ's actual provenance; no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics detected across any of the 5 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: Purely a screen-analysis research tool; no diagnostic, prescriptive, or individual-patient claims in any output.

methodological_ground.detail: Core method description (bidirectional Z-score, vehicle-anchored not Day-0) was empirically verified correct on real+synthetic data across all 5 inputs; no principled statistical fallacy found.

code_usability.detail: All CLI invocations documented in SKILL.md/usage-guide ran without syntax errors or missing dependencies (patched drugZ, 5/5 executions). Input 2's bundled essentials-exclusion example has a serious silent logic bug (0/684 genes actually excluded) but does not meet M4's strict 'unrunnable' bar -- it exits 0 with no exception. Scored heavily under the Data Analysis specialized rubric instead and flagged as a P0 recommendation.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness and appropriateness strong (standard run, dose designs, essentials exclusion, MAGeCK MLE comparison, failure-mode table all covered and correctly scoped to drugZ's real use case). Correctness docked: the only executable example for essentials-exclusion (examples/run_drugz.py Step 2) is silently broken -- verified to remove 0/684 genes.

reliability.note: No guidance covers the half_window_size/total-guide-count crash (Input 5, confirmed IndexError even at half_window_size=2 on a 9-guide table), and the essentials-exclusion no-op (Input 2) produces zero signal that anything failed -- exits 0, writes a complete-looking file.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md ~254 lines with a separate usage-guide and one example script; reasonable progressive disclosure, workflow is linear with no redundant steps.

agent_usability.note: Terminology and output-column documentation are exact matches to real drugZ output (verified). Error Prevention docked: the Failure Modes table covers Day-0-vs-vehicle and essentials-inflating-null well (both empirically confirmed real) but omits the half_window_size crash entirely, and does not flag that its own bundled -r example is broken.

human_usability.note: Natural-language trigger phrasing in usage-guide's Quick Start / Example Prompts is strong. Forgiveness scored under the Category-3 override (strict validation is a data-integrity guarantee, not a defect); scored down because there is no validation step at all before the small-library crash, not because strictness itself is penalized.

security.note: No credentials or PHI involved. Input Validation docked: examples/run_drugz.py never validates that -r's gene list actually parsed into real gene symbols, which is exactly how the silent no-op in Input 2 goes undetected.

maintainability.note: Clean SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples split. Testability docked: the essentials-exclusion example has no self-check (e.g. comparing output row/gene counts) that would have caught its own bug.

agent_specific.note: Precise, well-differentiated trigger description vs MAGeCK/BAGEL2; explicit Related Skills cross-references; deterministic/idempotent CLI. Escape Hatches docked: no guidance on what to do when a run crashes or when replicate Pearson is below the stated 0.85 threshold beyond listing it as a checklist item.

key_strengths: Canonical vehicle-vs-drug CLI invocation ran unmodified from SKILL.md and recovered 12/12 planted synthetic sensitizer+suppressor genes at ranks 1-6 each, with zero NaN/garbage values across 18,054 genes -- confirms both the patched drugZ CoW fix and the Skill's documented workflow work correctly end to end.

The Skill's central warning (compare drug to vehicle, never Day-0) is not just plausible advice: substituting Day-0 for vehicle empirically masked all 6 true hits (dropping them from rank 1-6 to rank ~700-1060) and produced 509 spurious 'significant' genes from proliferation drift alone.
Dose-response guidance (per-dose drugZ + consistency check) is methodologically correct and reproduces the expected weaker-but-same-direction signal at a simulated mid-dose.
Honest, literature-grounded positioning against MAGeCK MLE/RRA (real citations: Colic 2019, Olivieri 2020, Behan 2019) with a concrete decision table rather than marketing claims.

recommendations.title: Bundled essentials-exclusion example silently excludes zero genes
recommendations.problem: examples/run_drugz.py's own Step 2 downloads the real CEGv2.txt (tab-separated, 3 columns, header row) and joins its raw lines with commas, then passes that string to drugz.py -r. -r splits on comma and does an exact isin() match, so tokens like 'AARS\tHGNC:20\t16' never match any real gene symbol. Verified empirically: 0/684 genes removed, and the 'CEG-excluded' output is byte-identical (max |normZ diff| = 0.0) to the unfiltered run, while the tool exits 0 and writes a complete-looking file.
recommendations.root_cause: The example assumes remove_essential.txt is one bare gene symbol per line (as SKILL.md's own inline cat> snippet shows) but the real curl-downloaded CEGv2.txt used earlier in the same script has a different, multi-column format, and nothing parses or validates it.
recommendations.fix: Parse CEGv2.txt properly (skip header line, split on tab, take column 0) before joining into the -r argument, and add a post-hoc sanity check that compares gene counts between the filtered and unfiltered outputs to catch a zero-exclusion no-op.

recommendations.title: No documented relationship between total guide count and --half_window_size
recommendations.problem: Running drugZ on a small (9-guide) count table crashes with an uncaught IndexError regardless of --half_window_size, down to a value of 2. SKILL.md only documents a 4-6 sgRNA/gene minimum for stable per-gene Z, never that the empirical-Bayes sliding window needs total guide count well above half_window_size.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's stability guidance conflates per-gene guide count with total-library guide count, which govern different parts of the algorithm.
recommendations.fix: Add a Common Errors row for 'IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds' with the fix: total sgRNA count must be well above --half_window_size (default 500; confirmed working at roughly total_guides >= 4x half_window_size on a 200-guide test); for small pilot/arrayed sub-libraries, lower --half_window_size proportionally or use MAGeCK MLE instead.

recommendations.title: Dose-response section's only code is unexecutable pseudocode
recommendations.problem: The multi-dose loop shown in the SKILL.md/usage-guide is a commented-out sketch (# def per_dose_drugz(doses_dict): ... # subprocess.run(...)) rather than runnable code; an agent must write the real implementation from scratch to follow this workflow.
recommendations.root_cause: The dose-response pattern was documented conceptually but never turned into a working example, unlike the standard-run and essentials-exclusion sections.
recommendations.fix: Complete per_dose_drugz into runnable code with a concrete consistency rule (e.g. same-sign normZ at 2+ doses with fdr<0.05 at the top dose).

recommendations.title: No numeric threshold given for cross-dose 'consistency'
recommendations.problem: 'Consistent direction across doses' is never quantified -- no minimum correlation, rank overlap, or magnitude-ratio bound.
recommendations.root_cause: Guidance stops at a qualitative rule while every other threshold in the Skill (FDR, Pearson, sgRNA count) is quantitative.
recommendations.fix: Add a concrete rule, e.g. 'same sign at all tested doses and fdr<0.05 at the highest dose', consistent with the Skill's other quantitative-threshold tables.
